options.A: Holy books contain detailed anatomical drawings
options.B: Clergy members check medical records during weekly services
options.C: Religious schools teach the surgical steps to students
options.D: Local elders falsely claim scriptures demand it for modesty

explanation: Exactly! Misinterpretations from community leaders make people think this harmful custom is a spiritual duty.

question: Why is teaching the family of a neurological patient just as important as teaching the patient?

options.A: Doctors refuse to talk to anyone except the patient's spouse
options.B: Family members are legally required to pass nursing board exams
options.C: Patients with brain disorders completely lose the ability to speak
options.D: Family members often provide long-term care at home after discharge

explanation: Once the patient goes home, the family usually takes over daily care. Training them well means the patient stays safe and healthy after leaving the hospital.

question: Why is assuming a community's health needs based only on past experience a major mistake?

options.A: Every community has unique conditions, and unverified assumptions lead to wasted resources
options.B: Illnesses never repeat themselves in the same geographic location twice
options.C: Community members prefer foreign nurses to local healthcare workers
options.D: Past experience is legally forbidden in public health practice

explanation: Relying on assumptions instead of current local data often results in interventions that do not match real community needs. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h2)

question: Which study type compares patients who have a specific illness with those who don't, checking to see what they were exposed to in the past?

options.A: Case-control study
options.B: Prospective cohort
options.C: Randomized experiment
options.D: Clinical trial

explanation: You've got this! A case-control study starts with the final outcome (like having the disease) and looks backward to compare who was exposed to a risk factor and who wasn't.

question: Why do blood collection sample tubes come with different colored tops?

options.A: They contain different chemical additives for specific tests
options.B: They indicate the date the tubes were manufactured
options.C: They show which department ordered the laboratory test
options.D: They represent the different sizes of the patient's veins

explanation: Those color codes are lifesavers! They tell you which additive (like anticoagulants or clot activators) is inside for specific lab investigations.

question: Which of these is NOT something a community health nurse should do when promoting family planning?

options.A: Ensuring client confidentiality during health consultations
options.B: Dispelling common myths regarding modern contraceptive safety
options.C: Providing accurate counseling on various birth control options
options.D: Forcing community members to adopt specific contraceptive devices

explanation: You got it! Family planning must always be a personal choice. Forcing anyone goes against nursing ethics and human rights.

question: Which of the following is NOT a major challenge faced by public health nurses in many parts of Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive availability of ultra-modern robotic surgery equipment
options.B: Navigating cultural barriers and vaccine hesitancy in communities
options.C: Funding shortages affecting routine immunization supplies
options.D: Infrastructural deficits and poor road networks in remote areas

explanation: Robotic surgery equipment is found in advanced tertiary centers, not primary health care settings, making it an incorrect challenge for public health nurses. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h7)

question: What does 'event-related sterility' mean for packaged instruments sitting in storage?

options.A: Sterility depends entirely on the specific time of day it was processed
options.B: Instruments lose their sterility the moment they are placed on a shelf
options.C: All items automatically expire exactly seven days after autoclaving
options.D: Items remain sterile until the packaging is damaged or exposed to moisture

explanation: Instead of worrying about a strict calendar expiration date, packs stay sterile as long as the packaging remains safe and dry!

question: Why do so many teenagers today end up low on vitamin D?

options.A: Consuming too many citrus fruits and juices
options.B: Drinking excessive amounts of plain water
options.C: Avoiding all forms of dietary protein
options.D: Spending less time outdoors in natural sunlight

explanation: You nailed it! Our bodies make vitamin D from sunlight on the skin. With more indoor time and screen sessions, teens get less natural sun exposure.

question: Besides movement, what other important job do joints do for the body?

options.A: Regulating body temperature
options.B: Producing red blood cells
options.C: Maintaining posture and skeletal alignment
options.D: Filtering waste products from the blood

explanation: Great job! Joints work hand-in-hand with your muscles to hold your skeleton upright and keep your posture steady.

question: What is the best diagnostic test for looking directly at stomach ulcers and taking tiny tissue samples?

options.A: Plain abdominal X-ray
options.B: Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy
options.C: Barium swallow radiography
options.D: Abdominal ultrasound

explanation: Well done! Passing a tiny camera down (endoscopy) lets the doctor see the stomach lining directly and take samples for tests.

question: Why is 'Right Evaluation' so important after giving a medication?

options.A: It fulfills the legal requirement for daily bed making
options.B: It proves to the hospital pharmacy that pills were used
options.C: It allows the nurse to change the prescribed dosage
options.D: It confirms if the drug achieved its therapeutic goal

explanation: Evaluation is just checking back in later to see if the medicine actually worked or if it caused any sneaky side effects!

question: What physical measurement must be monitored closely when a newborn is suspected of having a subgaleal hemorrhage?

options.A: Abdominal girth
options.B: Chest expansion
options.C: Crown-to-heel length
options.D: Head circumference

explanation: Continuous accumulation of blood beneath the scalp increases the head size, making serial head circumference measurements essential for early detection. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T16#GNS121_U6_T16_h4)

question: What makes SIMV (Synchronized Intermittent Mandatory Ventilation) different from Assist-Control mode?

options.A: It delivers higher pressures with every single breath taken
options.B: It removes the need for any humidification system
options.C: It completely stops the patient from taking independent breaths
options.D: It allows the patient to breathe spontaneously between mandatory machine breaths

explanation: SIMV gives scheduled breaths but lets the patient do some of the work on their own in between. It's fantastic for exercising their respiratory muscles when they are getting stronger!

question: What makes a competitive antagonist unique?

options.A: It destroys the agonist molecules inside the bloodstream
options.B: It binds to a completely different site on the cell
options.C: It fights with the agonist for the same receptor site
options.D: It changes the chemical structure of the target organ

explanation: Competitive means they are wrestling for the exact same parking spot (receptor site)! Whoever gets there first or has more numbers wins the spot.

question: What is a great play activity for an infant in Gallows traction?

options.A: Taking them out for a crawling race
options.B: Placing heavy building blocks on their bed tray
options.C: Encouraging them to kick a small football
options.D: Hanging soft toys where they can easily see them

explanation: Since the baby is flat on their back, colourful mobiles and soft hanging toys keep their mind busy and happy without messing up the traction!

question: What is the primary site for nutrient absorption in the human body?

options.A: Stomach
options.B: Small intestine
options.C: Esophagus
options.D: Large intestine

explanation: The small intestine has specialized structures that provide a massive surface area specifically designed for taking in digested nutrients. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T7#GNS121_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why might a nurse choose dry heat sterilization instead of an autoclave for certain sharp tools or powders?

options.A: Dry heat uses steam pressure to penetrate thick plastic wrappers
options.B: Dry heat takes only two minutes to complete a full cycle
options.C: Dry heat is much cheaper to operate than electricity
options.D: Dry heat does not cause rusting or damage to moisture-sensitive items

explanation: Steam can rust fine metal edges or ruin powders. Dry heat is a wonderful alternative when you need to avoid moisture!

question: What is an early sign of HIV-related changes in thinking and memory?

options.A: Sudden total paralysis of the lower limbs
options.B: Mild mental slowing and poor concentration
options.C: Auditory hallucinations and fixed delusions
options.D: Complete and permanent loss of speech

explanation: Early on, patients might just notice it's harder to focus, remember things, or think as quickly as usual.

question: Why is strict sterile (aseptic) technique so important during a paracentesis?

options.A: To help the puncture site heal without a scar
options.B: To stop the patient from moving around
options.C: To make the local anesthetic work much faster
options.D: To prevent introducing bacteria into the abdomen

explanation: Keeping everything sterile ensures we don't accidentally push germs from the skin into the sterile belly cavity.

question: Why is it important to involve local leaders early in a health intervention?

options.A: Their endorsement helps build community trust and cooperation
options.B: It stops ordinary citizens from asking questions
options.C: They are required by law to pay for all medical equipment
options.D: They must personally diagnose every sick patient

explanation: Local populations listen closely to their leaders, making their backing crucial for high community participation. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h4)

question: When does intrapartum transmission of HIV primarily take place?

options.A: Through breast milk during the first week of life
options.B: As the baby passes through the birth canal
options.C: Across the placenta during the first trimester
options.D: Via airborne droplets in the delivery room

explanation: Intrapartum transmission happens when the infant is exposed to infected maternal blood and vaginal fluids during labor and birth. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h2)

question: A patient with a history of epilepsy comes to the clinic reporting frequent seizures after spending a week studying all night for exams. Which trigger is most likely responsible?

options.A: Genetic mutation
options.B: Flashing lights
options.C: Sleep deprivation
options.D: Cerebral infection

explanation: Severe lack of rest significantly lowers the brain's seizure threshold and is a very common trigger for acute attacks. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h4)

question: Why must public health nurses examine social and economic factors in a community?

options.A: Patients demand financial audits before receiving nursing care
options.B: These factors strongly influence overall health outcomes and disease patterns
options.C: Hospital administrators require these statistics for daily bed management
options.D: It helps doctors prescribe the correct brand of medication

explanation: Social and economic conditions shape the health status of populations, making them vital considerations for public health interventions. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h1)

question: What surgical procedure is often necessary during childbirth for a woman with Type III FGM?

options.A: Hysterectomy
options.B: Oophorectomy
options.C: Cervical cerclage
options.D: Defibulation

explanation: Brilliant! Defibulation means carefully cutting open the scar tissue seal so the mother can have a safe delivery and examination.

question: A patient with severe ulcerative colitis is having 10 bloody stools a day. What nursing action should you prioritize first?

options.A: Preparing the patient for heavy weight-lifting exercises
options.B: Monitoring intake and output and checking for signs of fluid loss
options.C: Encouraging a high-fiber raw vegetable diet to bulk up stool
options.D: Teaching the patient how to care for a permanent colostomy

explanation: You got it! Losing so much fluid through frequent diarrhea puts the patient at high risk for dehydration, making fluid tracking our top priority.

question: What is the main reason nurses practice emergency obstetric simulation drills?

options.A: To reduce the financial budget allocated for medical supplies
options.B: To help staff react calmly and swiftly during life-threatening crises
options.C: To test the durability of hospital furniture and delivery beds
options.D: To replace traditional nursing school lectures permanently

explanation: Practice makes perfect! Drills build your muscle memory and confidence so that when a real emergency happens, you stay cool and save lives. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h6)

question: Why are nurses uniquely positioned to perform effective infection surveillance?

options.A: They perform all terminal room cleaning procedures
options.B: They spend the most direct time at the patient's bedside
options.C: They are solely responsible for writing hospital policy
options.D: They process laboratory blood cultures in the hospital lab

explanation: Continuous bedside interaction allows nurses to spot early warning signs of infection long before lab results return. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h9)

question: Why is exogenous insulin therapy required for clients diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes?

options.A: Their kidneys rapidly destroy all oral medications before they reach cells
options.B: Their stomach acid inactivates any dietary carbohydrates they consume
options.C: Their liver stores too much glycogen that oral pills cannot break down
options.D: Their pancreas has undergone autoimmune destruction and produces no insulin

explanation: Because Type 1 diabetes involves a total lack of internal insulin production, patients must receive insulin from an outside source to survive. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h6)

question: What is the typical age range for early adolescence?

options.A: 10 to 13 years
options.B: 18 to 21 years
options.C: 6 to 9 years
options.D: 14 to 17 years

explanation: Early adolescence generally covers the ages of 10 to 13, marked heavily by the onset of puberty. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T3#GNS312_U3_T3_h2)

question: What do we mean by 'second victim syndrome' in healthcare?

options.A: A secondary illness caught by a patient while staying in the ward
options.B: Emotional trauma experienced by a clinician after being involved in an error
options.C: The legal penalty given to a hospital following a malpractice lawsuit
options.D: The family member who has to pay extra hospital bills for an injury

explanation: Nurses and doctors who go through a tough adverse event often carry deep emotional pain. We call them the second victims.

question: What is a major risk for a surgical patient whose stress is left unmanaged after an operation?

options.A: Decreased need for pain medication because adrenaline numbs nerves
options.B: Rapid healing caused by continuous high cortisol output
options.C: Lowered blood pressure preventing any risk of postoperative bleeding
options.D: Increased risk of infection due to suppressed immune function

explanation: When stress hormones stay high, they weaken the immune system, making it much easier for post-op patients to pick up infections. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h8)

question: What are the common signs of a Chlamydia infection in a young female?

options.A: Painless hard sores on the palms
options.B: High fever and generalized skin rash
options.C: Severe joint swelling and stiffness
options.D: Mucopurulent discharge and dysuria

explanation: Spot on! Chlamydia often causes irritation in the cervix and urethra, leading to unusual discharge and painful urination (dysuria).

question: Why is it important for nurses to involve local leaders when introducing a new immunization campaign?

options.A: Local leaders are legally required to sign off on all nursing licenses
options.B: It prevents nurses from having to buy their own medical supplies
options.C: Local leaders help build trust and encourage community members to participate
options.D: It ensures the village council pays the nurses' salaries

explanation: Community leaders hold influence and respect, making them vital bridges for gaining community acceptance and trust. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h4)

question: What major change happens to the spine in advanced ankylosing spondylitis?

options.A: Cartilage between discs completely dissolves and leaks
options.B: Vertebrae fuse together into a rigid structure
options.C: Spinal nerves swell and permanently pinch the spinal cord
options.D: Bones become overly soft and prone to micro-fractures

explanation: Over time, chronic inflammation causes the small bones of the spine (vertebrae) to grow together and fuse, making the spine completely rigid like a bamboo stick.

question: What bedside tool do nurses use to check the depth of a patient's muscle relaxation?

options.A: Bedside blood glucose meter
options.B: Peripheral nerve stimulator
options.C: Manual blood pressure cuff
options.D: Incentive spirometry device

explanation: A peripheral nerve stimulator gives tiny, safe zaps to check nerve and muscle response (the train-of-four test). Great tool for safe nursing care!

question: What does 'accessibility' mean when we talk about community health services?

options.A: Services are restricted to wealthy individuals who can pay cash
options.B: Care reaches marginalized and remote populations without discrimination
options.C: Clinics remain closed on weekends to protect staff schedules
options.D: Patients must travel long distances to reach urban tertiary centers

explanation: Well done! Accessibility means making sure that healthcare breaks down barriers—whether financial or geographical—so that everyone who needs care can actually get it.

question: An elderly patient on a fixed income is skipping meals to afford prescription drugs. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Provide a strict diet chart filled with expensive organic superfoods
options.B: Connect the patient with local food assistance programs and a social worker
options.C: Advise the patient to start a vigorous workout routine to boost appetite
options.D: Tell the patient to stop buying medications and spend money only on food

explanation: Linking vulnerable patients to community resources and social workers helps fix the root cause of their food insecurity. Amazing clinical thinking!

question: Why is it strongly preferred to give vasopressors through a central line rather than a peripheral vein?

options.A: Leaking into surrounding tissues can cause severe tissue damage and necrosis
options.B: Central lines deliver medication directly to the kidneys faster
options.C: Vasopressors dissolve peripheral plastic catheters very quickly
options.D: Peripheral veins are completely unable to absorb liquid medications

explanation: Vasopressors cause such intense blood vessel constriction that any leakage outside a peripheral vein cuts off local blood supply and destroys tissue. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h7)

question: What is the main goal of rehabilitation for a patient with a physical disability?

options.A: Optimal functional levels and independence
options.B: Permanent reliance on institutional care
options.C: Complete reversal of the underlying disease
options.D: Elimination of all chronic medications

explanation: Well done! Rehabilitation is all about helping a patient build on what they can still do, so they can live as independently as possible. You've got this!

question: Why do fat-soluble hormones need carrier proteins to travel in the blood?

options.A: Carrier proteins are needed to digest the hormone
options.B: They do not mix well with the watery plasma
options.C: They are too heavy to float without assistance
options.D: They would instantly destroy red blood cells if free

explanation: Oil and water don't mix! Since fat-soluble hormones don't dissolve in watery blood plasma, they need special carrier proteins to give them a ride through the circulatory system.

question: What does prevalence measure in a community?

options.A: The total number of existing disease cases
options.B: The number of deaths caused by an illness
options.C: The rate at which a disease spreads rapidly
options.D: The number of new infections starting today

explanation: Prevalence counts all existing cases, both old and new, in a population at a specific time. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h1)

question: Which vital sign must you always check before giving a combined hormonal contraceptive?

options.A: Respiratory rate
options.B: Temperature reading
options.C: Blood pressure
options.D: Oxygen saturation

explanation: Always check BP first! Estrogen can push blood pressure up and increase heart risks in vulnerable clients.

question: Why is it important for a nurse to tell normal sadness apart from clinical depression during an assessment?

options.A: To follow strict discharge rules set by the hospital administration
options.B: To prove to the family that the patient is faking their illness
options.C: To ensure the patient gets the right psychological or medical support
options.D: To avoid giving the patient any medications that lower blood pressure

explanation: It's normal to feel sad when facing a serious illness, but if it crosses into clinical depression, specialized counseling or treatment can truly help.

question: In what year was the historic Alma-Ata Declaration on Primary Health Care adopted?
explanation: The landmark international conference that defined Primary Health Care took place in Alma-Ata in 1978. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h1)

question: How is the grey matter and white matter arranged inside the developing spinal cord?

options.A: White matter forms internally and gray matter forms externally
options.B: Sensory fibers are kept completely outside the spinal column
options.C: Gray matter forms internally and white matter forms externally
options.D: Motor neurons develop only within the outer white matter

explanation: Great thinking! The spinal cord is neatly organized with nerve cell bodies on the inside (grey matter) and nerve fiber tracts on the outside (white matter).

question: What sensation should you warn a patient to expect when the barium liquid goes in?

options.A: Total numbness from the waist down to the toes
options.B: Heavy sleepiness and deep drowsiness
options.C: A sharp burning feeling across the skin of the belly
options.D: A strong urge to use the toilet and mild belly cramps

explanation: Filling the large intestine with fluid naturally creates pressure and triggers bowel contractions. Giving patients a heads-up helps ease their anxiety.

question: How does poverty directly affect a pregnant woman's health outcomes?

options.A: It forces healthcare providers to deny them basic vaccinations
options.B: It completely stops the placenta from producing progesterone and estrogen
options.C: It restricts their ability to afford transport and hospital fees during emergencies
options.D: It guarantees that they will develop gestational diabetes late in the third trimester

explanation: Financial barriers can prevent women from reaching skilled medical facilities when urgent complications arise. It's a reminder of why accessible healthcare is so vital.

question: A patient taking warfarin has a dangerously high INR and mild bleeding. What will the medical team most likely give?

options.A: Aspirin
options.B: Iron tablets
options.C: Vitamin K
options.D: Heparin

explanation: Since warfarin blocks Vitamin K, giving extra Vitamin K is the direct antidote to reverse its effects and restore normal clotting.

question: A student nurse notices patients often get confused when discharged without written instructions. Why is this a valid research problem?

options.A: It highlights a communication gap that affects patient safety and outcomes
options.B: It proves that patients are entirely at fault for forgetting instructions
options.C: It shows that written paper is more expensive than digital tablets
options.D: It demonstrates that discharge rounds are unnecessary tasks

explanation: Discharge confusion puts patient recovery at risk. Studying how to fix this communication gap is super important for safe nursing!

question: What is a major spatial or geographical challenge for patients living in remote rural areas?

options.A: Long distances and poor roads making it difficult to reach health facilities
options.B: Too many doctors competing for patients in remote farming settlements
options.C: Excessive electricity supply causing medical equipment to overheat
options.D: An overabundance of specialized tertiary hospitals in small villages

explanation: That's right! Bad roads and long distances make traveling to a clinic a huge hurdle for rural residents.

question: What is the leading cause of ongoing back pain and injuries among nursing staff?

options.A: Writing patient reports while sitting on unadjusted chairs
options.B: Walking across slippery hospital floors in soft shoes
options.C: Lifting and moving heavy patients without proper mechanical assistance
options.D: Standing still at the nursing station during long night shifts

explanation: Pulling or lifting heavy patients manually puts massive strain on your lower back. Always use proper leverage, help, or lifting devices!

question: Why are fats so great for energy storage?

options.A: Fats yield more than twice the calories per gram compared to carbs
options.B: Fats do not require enzymes to be broken down in the stomach
options.C: Fats can be turned into glucose instantly without any waste products
options.D: Fats dissolve directly in water without needing transport proteins

explanation: Lipids are super compact energy bundles, packing more than double the punch (calories) per gram than carbs or proteins!

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse can do to treat a genetic degenerative disorder?

options.A: Evaluating bowel patterns to prevent severe constipation
options.B: Administering a daily cure to reverse genetic mutations
options.C: Assessing respiratory effort and cough strength regularly
options.D: Monitoring skin integrity for signs of pressure injury

explanation: Right now, we can't rewrite someone's DNA. Our nursing care focuses completely on keeping them comfortable and preventing complications.

question: How are Wernicke encephalopathy and Korsakoff syndrome related?

options.A: They are completely unrelated disorders affecting different organs
options.B: Korsakoff syndrome always occurs years before Wernicke develops
options.C: Wernicke is a mild form of memory loss caused by normal aging
options.D: Wernicke is the acute stage and Korsakoff is the chronic stage

explanation: They are actually two sides of the same coin! Wernicke is the sudden, early emergency phase, and Korsakoff is the long-term memory issue that follows if it's not treated quickly.

question: Why might an adolescent with untreated depression turn to substance abuse?

options.A: To cure a bacterial infection
options.B: To improve their school grades permanently
options.C: To self-medicate and escape emotional pain
options.D: To strengthen their immune system

explanation: Teens struggling with mental health issues like depression often use drugs or alcohol as an unhealthy way to cope with overwhelming emotional distress. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T13#GNS312_U3_T13_h3)

question: What should the nurse apply across the incision after removing sutures to provide extra support?

options.A: Sterile adhesive strips
options.B: Tight elastic bandages
options.C: Thick plaster of paris
options.D: Wet saline gauze pads

explanation: Adhesive closure strips help hold the skin edges together gently while the deeper layers continue gaining strength after suture removal. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h6)

question: Why is a delicate balance of hemostasis important for a patient?

options.A: It maintains the proper blood pH balance during heavy exercise
options.B: It controls the exact amount of iron absorbed from the diet
options.C: It prevents both uncontrolled bleeding and unwanted blood clots
options.D: It ensures the heart rate stays within a normal resting range

explanation: The body must carefully balance clotting so that injuries seal properly without forming dangerous blockages inside healthy vessels. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is the main goal of antiretroviral therapy (ART) for someone living with HIV?

options.A: Suppressing the viral load and protecting immune function
options.B: Stimulating the immediate production of thick mucosal barriers
options.C: Permanently killing all virus particles within the bone marrow
options.D: Preventing the development of seasonal respiratory allergies

explanation: Spot on! ART keeps the virus levels super low, which keeps the immune system strong and healthy.

question: A patient with an endotracheal tube needs suctioning when which sign appears?

options.A: Warm, dry skin with pink nail beds
options.B: Audible or visible secretions in the airway tube
options.C: Deep, quiet breathing sounds in all lung fields
options.D: A normal, steady heart rate and blood pressure

explanation: Seeing or hearing mucus rattling in the tube tells the nurse the airway is partially blocked and needs clearing. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h2)

question: When should a nurse apply standard precautions during patient care?

options.A: When working exclusively in surgical operating theaters
options.B: Only after a laboratory confirms a bloodborne pathogen
options.C: Only when caring for patients with confirmed viral infections
options.D: During the care of all patients regardless of their diagnosis

explanation: Standard precautions treat all body fluids as potentially infectious and must be used for every patient every time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h4)

question: What happens if a nurse shakes a vial of reconstituted medication too vigorously?

options.A: The active ingredients in the medication instantly multiply
options.B: The medicine changes color to indicate it is ready
options.C: Excessive foam and bubbles form, making accurate measurement difficult
options.D: The glass vial shatters due to rapid temperature changes

explanation: Vigorous shaking whips air into the liquid, creating foam and bubbles that distort volume measurements inside the syringe. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T22#GNS122_U1_T22_h5)

question: Why does chronic straining often lead to the development of hemorrhoids?

options.A: It increases pressure on the blood vessels around the anus
options.B: It strips the protective mucous layer off the colon
options.C: It stops the liver from filtering blood properly
options.D: It causes rapid dehydration of the entire body

explanation: Straining forces extra blood into the rectal and anal veins, causing them to swell and form hemorrhoids. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h3)

question: A new mum is worried about being very forgetful two weeks after giving birth. What should you do?

options.A: Refer her immediately for a complex magnetic resonance imaging scan of the brain
options.B: Notify the primary physician that she is showing signs of early-onset dementia
options.C: Instruct her to stop breastfeeding immediately to restore normal vitamin levels
options.D: Reassure her that temporary cognitive shifts and memory lapses are normal adaptive changes

explanation: Be her comfort! Postpartum 'brain fog' is totally normal as the brain adjusts. Reassuring her goes a long way in easing her anxiety.

question: Why is using good, clear logic so important from the beginning to the end of your research?

options.A: It guarantees the hospital will fund the research project
options.B: It ensures conclusions directly match the gathered evidence
options.C: It removes the need for any statistical calculations
options.D: It stops patients from withdrawing from the study

explanation: Spot on! Sound logic stops us from making wild claims that our actual data doesn't back up. Keep it logical!

question: Where do the testicular arteries originate from?

options.A: Renal vein branch
options.B: Femoral artery
options.C: Internal iliac artery
options.D: Abdominal aorta

explanation: Because the testes form near the kidneys during embryonic development before descending, their main blood supply stems directly from the abdominal aorta. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h7)

question: A patient comes in with a 'buffalo hump' of fat, a round belly, and purple stretch marks on their skin. Which condition matches these signs?

options.A: Hypothyroidism
options.B: Cushing's disease
options.C: Acromegaly
options.D: Diabetes insipidus

explanation: These classic changes happen when the body is flooded with too much cortisol. In Cushing's disease, this is often kicked off by a tiny pituitary tumor pushing out extra ACTH.

question: Which sign do we often see when a patient is in the final active dying phase?

options.A: Warm, flushed skin over the entire body
options.B: Irregular breathing patterns like Cheyne-Stokes respirations
options.C: Rapid increase in blood pressure and heart rate
options.D: Sudden increase in appetite and high energy levels

explanation: As the body gently slows down, you might notice cool hands and feet, sleeping more, and irregular breathing patterns like Cheyne-Stokes. Knowing this helps you reassure the family.

question: Why should a nurse take every report of cramping in pregnancy seriously?

options.A: Milder aches can sometimes mask or precede serious complications.
options.B: All pregnant women require immediate bed rest for any pain.
options.C: Pain medications are mandatory for any reported discomfort.
options.D: Cramping always indicates an active uterine infection.

explanation: Even though most cramps are completely normal, checking them out helps us make sure we don't miss important warning signs like an ectopic pregnancy or preterm labor. Great nursing instincts!

question: Which everyday or routine activity carries a real risk of transmitting HIV?

options.A: Sharing eating utensils and drinking cups at a family dinner
options.B: Sharing intravenous drug injection needles with an infected person
options.C: Receiving a hug or handshake from an infected coworker
options.D: Swimming in the same public pool as a person with HIV

explanation: HIV spreads through direct blood-to-blood contact, such as sharing needles. Casual contact like hugging or sharing spoons is completely safe!

question: Why do inhaled anesthetic gases exit the body so quickly through the lungs?

options.A: They easily cross the tiny air sacs (alveoli) from the blood right into the lungs.
options.B: Inhaled gases bind tightly to red blood cells until reaching the lungs.
options.C: The kidneys cannot filter gases, so the lungs are the only option.
options.D: Lung tissue actively pumps anesthetic molecules out into the room air.

explanation: Once a patient stops breathing the anesthesia gas, the gas dissolved in their blood naturally crosses the thin air sac membranes when they exhale, clearing it out fast.

question: What should a client do if she misses one combined pill by more than 12 hours?

options.A: Take three pills at once on the following morning
options.B: Take the missed pill right away and continue the rest as normal
options.C: Throw away the entire packet and wait for her next period
options.D: Stop taking birth control pills for the rest of that month

explanation: Don't panic over one missed pill! Just take the missed one immediately and keep going with the pack as usual. Protection is usually still intact.

question: How do modified utensils with built-in grips help a patient with failing fine motor control?

options.A: They compensate for weak grip strength and hand tremors
options.B: They completely cure the underlying nerve degeneration
options.C: They prevent the patient from feeling hungry
options.D: They make the food taste better and digest faster

explanation: Specialized grips provide better purchase for weak hands, allowing the patient to continue feeding themselves without assistance. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h5)

question: What instruction should a nurse give a patient after inserting a retention suppository?

options.A: Drink two liters of ice-cold water within five minutes
options.B: Force an immediate bowel movement to test if it worked
options.C: Try to remain lying down and hold the medication for 15 to 30 minutes
options.D: Get up immediately and walk briskly around the hospital hallway

explanation: Giving the medication time to dissolve and absorb into the mucosal lining prevents it from being prematurely expelled. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h8)

question: On a baby's head, what is the area located between the bridge of the nose and the front soft spot called?

options.A: Face
options.B: Occiput
options.C: Brow
options.D: Vertex

explanation: You're doing great! The brow sits right above the eyes and nose. If a baby tries to be born brow-first, it makes for a tricky delivery because that part is quite wide.

question: How might a depressed older adult unusually show their emotional pain?

options.A: By writing poetry about deep emotional sorrow
options.B: By expressing intense excitement about the future
options.C: Through vague physical aches and sleep problems
options.D: Through sudden bursts of aggressive athletic activity

explanation: Older adults often express sadness through bodily aches and trouble sleeping rather than saying 'I feel depressed.' Good to know!

question: Why do hospitals use standard clinical protocols?

options.A: To increase the paperwork load for night shift nurses
options.B: To eliminate all forms of natural patient diversity
options.C: To ensure every patient recovers in the exact same timeframe
options.D: To reduce unwanted differences in patient care

explanation: You've got this! Standardized protocols simply help guide our practice so that every patient gets safe, consistent care no matter who is on duty. Keep it up!

question: How does human placental lactogen primarily help the developing fetus?

options.A: By directly oxygenating fetal blood within the intervillous space
options.B: By altering maternal metabolism to make more glucose available
options.C: By preventing maternal antibodies from attacking fetal tissues
options.D: By lubricating the birth canal in preparation for vaginal delivery

explanation: Placental lactogen acts as an antagonist to maternal insulin, ensuring that glucose stays in the bloodstream longer so it can readily cross over to nourish the fetus. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h1)

question: What is the real difference between just hearing someone talk and active listening?

options.A: Active listening can only be performed in a quiet hospital office.
options.B: Hearing requires the nurse to offer immediate medical diagnoses.
options.C: Active listening involves full concentration on both words and underlying emotions.
options.D: Hearing requires the nurse to write down every spoken word verbatim.

explanation: Active listening means tuning into the feelings behind the words, not just waiting for your turn to speak. Great nurses master this!

question: A patient is pacing the ward rapidly, breathing fast, and speaking in a frantic rush. What should you do first?

options.A: Administer a strong oral stimulant to boost their energy.
options.B: Move the patient to a quiet area and speak in a calm, reassuring tone.
options.C: Leave the patient alone until they calm down on their own.
options.D: Ask the patient to sit down and fill out a detailed anxiety questionnaire.

explanation: Lowering the noise and distractions around the patient—paired with your own calm presence—does wonders to bring their anxiety down.

question: A doctor prescribes a proton pump inhibitor to a patient with a stomach ulcer. What is the goal of this medicine?

options.A: Reduced stomach acid production to promote ulcer healing
options.B: Increased release of bile to speed up fat digestion
options.C: Stimulation of the vagus nerve to increase appetite
options.D: Enhanced production of mucus by goblet cells

explanation: By shutting down those acid pumps, the stomach environment becomes less acidic, giving the sore tissue a chance to rest and heal up nicely. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T12#GNS121_U1_T12_h7)

question: What is a common long-term physical problem caused by having very heavy periods for a long time?

options.A: Permanent kidney failure
options.B: Iron-deficiency anemia
options.C: Broken bones
options.D: Severe adult asthma

explanation: You nailed it! Losing blood month after month empties out the body's iron reserves, leading directly to anemia.

question: What is the main nursing priority right after delivery for a patient who had placenta accreta?

options.A: Monitoring for signs of postpartum hemorrhage and shock
options.B: Administering oral iron supplements for mild fatigue
options.C: Encouraging immediate ambulation around the ward
options.D: Preparing the infant for immediate nursery discharge

explanation: Because accreta makes it hard for the uterus to contract properly and clear all tissue, keeping a close eye on bleeding is your number one lifesaving duty. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h8)

question: Why won't hormonal emergency pills work if a woman has already ovulated?

options.A: Because the hormone dose is too low to stay in the stomach
options.B: Because the egg has already been released and is available for fertilization
options.C: Because ovulation automatically neutralizes all chemical drugs
options.D: Because the uterine lining instantly sheds upon ovulation

explanation: Remember, these pills work by delaying ovulation. If the egg has already been released, the pill is too late to stop it from meeting a sperm. Makes total sense, right?

question: What is the main goal of the Drug Revolving Fund (DRF) model in public hospitals?

options.A: To replace state government health budgets entirely
options.B: To fund free housing for incoming medical staff
options.C: To ensure a steady supply of essential medicines
options.D: To generate heavy profit for hospital management

explanation: You've got this! The DRF uses money from drug sales strictly to restock those same drugs, keeping our pharmacy shelves stocked so we never run out unexpectedly.

question: Why would a cell decide to do receptor downregulation?

options.A: To help absorb more nutrients directly from the bloodstream
options.B: To protect itself from being overstimulated by high hormone levels
options.C: To prepare the cell to divide into two identical daughter cells
options.D: To allow fat-soluble hormones to cross the cell wall faster

explanation: If there's way too much hormone around for too long, the cell pulls some receptors inside to take a break and avoid getting overwhelmed. Smart cells know their limits! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T11#GNS211_U1_T11_h2)

question: Why are healthcare workers sometimes at higher risk for developing substance use issues?

options.A: They are completely exempt from the legal penalties of drug abuse
options.B: They experience heavy job stress and have easy access to medications
options.C: They receive special training on how to safely consume illegal substances
options.D: They possess a genetic immunity that makes them careless with drugs

explanation: The intense stress of clinical life combined with being around drugs all day creates a tough environment. Looking out for our mental health as nurses is so important!

question: A nurse notices that new mothers in the postnatal ward look anxious about breastfeeding. Which option turns this into a well-focused research study?

options.A: Asking every nurse on the ward how they feel about their personal jobs
options.B: Reviewing the financial cost of building a new maternity ward
options.C: Studying why the entire healthcare system in the country is failing mothers
options.D: Evaluating whether a peer support group lowers anxiety scores among first-time breastfeeding mothers

explanation: Spot on! This takes a real ward observation (breastfeeding anxiety) and turns it into a clear, measurable plan with a specific group of people.

question: What is the most effective way for a nurse to interview a suspected victim of breast ironing?

options.A: In a busy hospital hallway in front of other visitors
options.B: By asking the mother to explain all the child's injuries
options.C: By waiting until the doctor completes a full physical exam
options.D: In a private room away from accompanying family members

explanation: Privacy is essential because accompanying relatives are often the perpetrators or supporters of the abuse. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T17#GNS312_U1_T17_h6)

question: What approach should a nurse use when caring for a patient experiencing complications from a harmful traditional practice?

options.A: Trauma-informed and non-judgmental care
options.B: Strict detachment with no emotional conversation
options.C: Refusal of treatment until legal charges are filed
options.D: Immediate public shaming to deter future acts

explanation: Patients must feel safe and respected to build trust and accept necessary medical and psychological support. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h6)

question: What is a major social reason families continue to practice FGM?

options.A: Compliance with international health mandates
options.B: A direct recommendation by the national medical association
options.C: The prevention of childhood infectious diseases
options.D: Fear of social exclusion and unmarriageability

explanation: Sadly, many families do it because they fear their daughters will be rejected by the community or struggle to find husbands. Understanding this helps you treat patients with empathy.

question: What is the main feature that separates stable angina from unstable angina?

options.A: Stable angina lasts for days without any relief
options.B: Unstable angina is always completely cured with exercise
options.C: Unstable angina occurs unpredictably even at rest
options.D: Stable angina causes pain that radiates down both legs

explanation: While stable angina follows a predictable pattern during exertion, unstable angina can happen at rest and represents a medical emergency. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h4)

question: What does the term 'legal liability' mean in nursing practice?

options.A: Being legally responsible for one's professional actions and omissions
options.B: The right to sue a client for refusing prescribed medication
options.C: The obligation to pay taxes on monthly nursing salaries
options.D: Having absolute immunity from all criminal charges in court

explanation: Liability means accountability under the law for the duties performed or neglected during professional practice. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h6)

question: Can an overweight patient still suffer from poor nutrition? If so, why?

options.A: Yes, because body weight doesn't show the quality of micronutrients consumed
options.B: Yes, because overweight people cannot absorb proteins at all
options.C: No, because excess body fat stores all necessary vitamins forever
options.D: No, because larger people always have fast metabolisms

explanation: A person can eat plenty of calories and still lack essential vitamins and minerals. That's hidden malnutrition!

question: Which measure is best for preventing cholera in a community over the long term?

options.A: Improving access to safe drinking water and sanitation
options.B: Administering daily preventive antibiotics to everyone
options.C: Isolating all infected patients in dark rooms
options.D: Spraying insecticides inside every household

explanation: Clean water and proper sewage disposal stop the bacteria from ever reaching our drinking sources. Public health at its best!

question: Why are LARC methods considered very effective for post-abortion contraception?

options.A: They completely stop all bacteria from entering the reproductive tract
options.B: They do not require daily action or memory from the user to prevent pregnancy
options.C: They destroy all male sperm cells before they reach the vagina
options.D: They can only be removed permanently by surgical removal of the uterus

explanation: Human error, like forgetting a pill, is a major cause of contraceptive failure, which LARC methods bypass entirely. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h4)

question: Which portable device does a patient wear to continuously send heart rhythm data to the nurse's station?

options.A: A standard mercury sphygmomanometer
options.B: A handheld blood glucose meter
options.C: A telemetry transmitter
options.D: A basic digital thermometer

explanation: Telemetry packs are worn by the patient to wirelessly beam their ECG rhythm straight to the central monitor. Very handy for cardiac patients!

question: Why do nurses take baseline neurological data when a patient is first admitted?

options.A: To compare with later findings to detect clinical changes
options.B: To calculate the patient's exact hospital discharge date
options.C: To determine the exact cause of a brain tumor
options.D: To replace the need for physician daily rounds

explanation: Having a clear starting point helps you quickly spot any tiny changes if the patient's condition starts to slip later!

question: Why would a doctor perform a therapeutic abortion?

options.A: Fulfilling an elective personal request without medical reason
options.B: Preventing multiple births during fertility treatments
options.C: Ending a pregnancy due to financial convenience alone
options.D: Protecting maternal health or addressing severe fetal anomalies

explanation: Therapeutic abortions are done to save the mother's life or health, or when the baby has very severe issues that mean it cannot survive.

question: What is the best reason to place a healthy newborn skin-to-skin on mum's chest right after birth?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need to dry the baby with warm towels
options.B: It allows the nurse to perform the complete physical head-to-toe exam faster
options.C: It prevents the infant from passing meconium before the placenta is delivered
options.D: It helps maintain the newborn's body temperature and encourages early breastfeeding

explanation: Mum's chest is like a natural incubator! Skin-to-skin keeps baby warm and wakes up those natural instincts to latch and breastfeed.

question: What is the recommended target range for endotracheal tube cuff pressure to prevent tracheal damage?

options.A: 60 to 70 cmH2O
options.B: 40 to 50 cmH2O
options.C: 20 to 30 cmH2O
options.D: 5 to 10 cmH2O

explanation: Maintaining cuff pressure between 20 and 30 cmH2O seals the airway adequately without cutting off blood flow to the tracheal lining. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h6)

question: What is the immediate impact of early marriage on a young girl's education?

options.A: Immediate promotion to higher academic grades
options.B: An abrupt end to her formal education
options.C: Free government-funded university placement
options.D: Mandatory transfer to an adult night school

explanation: Spot on! Heavy household chores and early pregnancies almost always force young brides to drop out of school for good.

question: Which of the following is a well-known risk factor for future violent behavior?

options.A: Consistently achieving a high level of formal education
options.B: Living in a household with little to no financial debt
options.C: Taking an active part in school or community sports
options.D: Experiencing abuse or trauma during childhood

explanation: Spot on! Early childhood trauma and seeing domestic abuse at home are strong warning signs for experiencing or committing violence later in life.

question: Why is the inner forearm a preferred site for routine tuberculosis skin tests?

options.A: It is hairless and allows easy visual inspection of the reaction.
options.B: It has a higher concentration of blood vessels for rapid results.
options.C: It contains thick subcutaneous fat that cushions the needle.
options.D: It absorbs medications much faster than other body parts.

explanation: The inner forearm provides a clear, accessible area with minimal hair, making it simple for nurses to read skin changes accurately. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is the main reason midwives and nurses use a partograph during active labor?

options.A: To record financial payments made by the patient at the hospital
options.B: To calculate the exact date of conception for the mother
options.C: To track labor progress and detect prolonged labor early
options.D: To determine the blood group and genotype of the newborn

explanation: The partograph is your trusty graphical roadmap of labor. It helps you spot when things are taking too long so you can act fast.

question: Why is it important to inspect MVA plastic syringes and canulas closely before sterilization?

options.A: To ensure the plastic has changed color indicating expiration
options.B: To check for cracks, scratches, or wear that could harbor bacteria
options.C: To verify the manufacturing country and brand name
options.D: To measure how much weight the plastic can hold under pressure

explanation: Damaged or cracked plastic instruments cannot maintain a proper vacuum and can trap microorganisms, leading to infection risks. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h8)

question: What should a nurse do when faced with an unclear or ambiguous prescription order?

options.A: Hold the drug for the entire day without telling anyone
options.B: Administer a standard average dose based on common practice
options.C: Ask a junior student nurse to guess what the doctor meant
options.D: Contact the prescriber immediately to clarify the exact instruction

explanation: Guessing an unclear order puts the patient at extreme risk; the prescribing clinician must always clarify ambiguous instructions. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h4)

question: How many weeks does a normal, full-term human pregnancy typically last?

options.A: 32 weeks
options.B: 40 weeks
options.C: 36 weeks
options.D: 44 weeks

explanation: A standard full-term gestation spans about 40 weeks from the start of the last menstrual period, or roughly 38 weeks from actual fertilization. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T001#GNS226_U2_T001_h4)

question: Why is community health nursing so important to primary health care in Nigeria?

options.A: It manages all tertiary hospital admissions across the country
options.B: It brings preventative and basic health services directly to local populations
options.C: It exclusively handles complex surgical procedures in rural areas
options.D: It replaces the need for doctors in government hospitals

explanation: You got it! By stepping into local clinics, schools, and homes, community health nurses make sure everyday preventative care actually reaches where people live.

question: What is the main goal of birth preparedness and complication readiness in pregnancy?

options.A: To eliminate the need for routine antenatal visits
options.B: To choose the exact time and date of labor
options.C: To remove delays in accessing emergency obstetric care
options.D: To guarantee a home delivery without any skilled staff

explanation: Planning ahead for transport and funds helps ensure a woman gets to the hospital fast if an emergency happens.
